battle.name: 七國之亂
battle.brief: 前154年正月，吳王劉濞、楚王劉戊等七國以「清君側」為名舉兵。漢廷遣周亞夫、竇嬰將三十六將軍東出，亞夫據昌邑深壁固守，竇嬰絕其糧道於淮泗，吳楚軍饑而潰，亞夫追擊大破之，楚王自縊，吳王走東越被殺。卡面亞述長矛早於本役一千二百餘年，它留下的是短柄長刃的刺擊譜系。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 七國之亂是前154年（漢景帝三年、元朔三年）正月爆發的一場諸侯王聯軍起兵。叛方是同姓七國王：吳王劉濞居首，領江淮之地，會稽郡已被削去；楚王劉戊以彭城為中心，握淮南與江南之兵；趙王劉建、齊王劉將閾分守北方與山東；齊王一系還有膠西王劉、菑川王劉賢、濟南王劉辟光三王相助，合稱七國。叛軍的口號是「誅晁錯、清君側」，真正的目標卻是保住王國的封土與兵權。朝廷一方是景帝劉啟為主的中央：丞相之權由御史大夫晁錯代行，中尉在東市行刑，外有竇氏與梁王劉武在朝中為吳國說話，使議兵的過程一再拖延。真正執兵的是奉詔東出的太尉周亞夫與大將軍竇嬰，兩軍合兵後由亞夫將三十六將軍往擊吳楚，竇嬰分兵斷其糧道，騎兵由輕騎司馬與材官校尉分領。收束戰局的除了中央的兩支部隊，還有地方郡縣的守令與東越的邊地武裝：吳王劉濞敗走東越，東越出兵將其斬首送漢。
countriesEn: The Revolt of the Seven States broke out in the first month of the third year of Emperor Jing of Han (154 BC, the third year of Yuanshou). The rebel side was a coalition of seven kings of the same clan: at their head the Prince of Wu Liu Pi, who held the lands along the Yangzi and the Huai but had already been stripped of the commandery of Kuaiji; the Prince of Chu Liu Wu, centred on Pengcheng, commanding the lands south of the Huai and across the river; the Prince of Zhao Liu Jian and the Prince of Qi Liu Jianglü holding the north and the shores of Shandong; and, joined to the Prince of Qi, the three kings of Jiaoxi, Zichuan and Jinan — the seven in all. The rebels marched under the slogan 'punish Chao Cuo and clear the side of the ruler', but the real purpose was to keep the fiefs and the armed forces of the kingdoms. On the court side stood the central government of Emperor Jing, Liu Qi, with the chancellor's office in fact exercised by the Imperial Secretary Chao Cuo and the Zhongwei executing judgements in the eastern market; outside the palace, the Dou clan and the Prince of Liang Liu Wu argued the cause of Wu at court, and the debate over sending troops was delayed again and again. The army that actually fought was the force dispatched east by the Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu and the General-in-Chief Dou Ying: joined together, Yafu took thirty-six generals against the armies of Wu and Chu, Dou Ying was detached to sever their supply line, and the horse were distributed under the light-horse commandant and the engineers of the mobile column. What closed the campaign was not only those two central columns but the commandery officials on the ground and the armed bands of Dongyue on the frontier: Liu Pi fled to Dongyue after his defeat, and Dongyue killed him and sent his head to Han.
people: 領兵與決策的人分在兩邊。叛方首謀是吳王劉濞，他以六十餘歲之齡起兵，先遣使約楚王劉戊，兩人互相推讓王位，約定一旦論功，誰為王便與誰分之；齊王劉將閾、趙王劉建隨之舉兵，膠西王劉、菑川王劉賢、濟南王劉辟光各自帶兵趨向漢境要地。齊國那幾位王的內部很快互咬：膠西、菑川二王圖謀齊王之位，齊王聞訊先發制人，兄弟反目成仇。朝廷一方，景帝劉啟在竇氏的壓力下猶豫不決，最後聽從袁盎之言，殺了御史大夫晁錯；晁錯在囚車上向左右申說，治國之臣本當為國事著言，如今主張不被採用，剩下的只有一死。殺掉晁錯，七國的兵並沒有罷，景帝這才下詔討伐，命周亞夫為太尉、竇嬰為大將軍往擊吳楚，又令梁王劉武固守睢陽。亞夫麾下軍侯趙賁獻策，說吳楚之兵輕進而無備，糧道空虛，應先據要地以老其師；亞夫從之，引兵東北走昌邑，深壁而守。竇嬰一部以騎兵屯於淮泗之間，斷吳楚的粟米通道。吳軍缺糧，士卒飢疲，聯軍退卻之際亞夫出精兵追擊，在退路上大破之。吳王劉濞丟下大軍，帶數千壯士逃入東越，東越隨即殺之，將首級送漢。楚王劉戊的部將勸他不要離開軍隊，劉戊不聽，兵散之後走投無路，最後自縊而死。齊王劉將閾與二弟膠西、菑川王同死於亂軍，趙王劉建、濟南王劉辟光相繼被擒或被殺，七國之王無一得脫。
peopleEn: The men who decided and fought fell into two camps. The first mover on the rebel side was the Prince of Wu, Liu Pi, who rose in the east of his realm at more than sixty years of age; he first sent envoys to the Prince of Chu, Liu Wu, and the two pushed the kingship back and forth between them, agreeing that whoever should be made king would hold it jointly. The Prince of Qi, Liu Jianglü, and the Prince of Zhao, Liu Jian, followed with their own risings, while the kings of Jiaoxi, Zichuan and Jinan led troops toward the strategic points of Han territory. Inside Qi the kings very soon turned on one another: the kings of Jiaoxi and Zichuan schemed for the throne of Qi, and the Prince of Qi, hearing of it, struck first, so that brothers became enemies. On the court's side, Emperor Jing hesitated under the pressure of the Dou clan and finally followed the advice of Yuan Ang and put the Imperial Secretary Chao Cuo to death; Chao Cuo, on the way to the eastern market in the prison cart, addressed the officers on either side, saying that the ministers of state had spoken for the good of the realm and that since their counsel had not been taken, nothing remained for him but death. Killing Chao Cuo did not stop the armies of the seven, and only then did Jing issue the order for suppression, naming Zhou Yafu Grand Commandant and Dou Ying General-in-Chief to march against Wu and Chu, and requiring the Prince of Liang Liu Wu to hold Shihyang. A military officer named Zhao Ben under Yafu's command proposed a plan: the troops of Wu and Chu came on lightly and were badly provisioned, their line of supply would lie open, and the Han army should seize the key ground first and wear the enemy down. Yafu took the plan, marched his force northeast to Changyi and shut himself in his works. Dou Ying's detachment posted horse between the Huai and the Si and cut the grain road of the rebels. The Wu-Chu army was short of food, the men were hungry and spent, and as the coalition withdrew Yafu sent his picked troops after it and broke it on the line of retreat. Liu Pi left his army behind and fled with a few thousand hard men; Dongyue killed him and sent his head to Han. The Chu king's generals urged Liu Wu not to abandon the army, but he refused, and when the ranks scattered he was cornered and hanged himself. The Prince of Qi and his two brothers, the kings of Jiaoxi and Zichuan, all died in the fighting they turned on one another; Liu Jian of Zhao and Liu Biguang of Jinan were taken or killed in turn, and not one of the seven kings escaped.
kits: 這場戰爭裡真正上手的兵器，與卡面那柄亞述長矛隔了九個半世紀。亞述長矛的形制是短柄、長刃，鐵鏃套在木桿上；兩河流域靠它守住城牆，也靠它撞開城牆，柄長與刃形都為密集隊形而定。到了西漢前154年，兵器譜系已經分岔：漢軍步卒用戟，長及丈許，可以刺、可以鉤、也可以擲落砸擊，配以大盾與札甲，近身纏鬥靠的是以長制短；射手另編，弓與弩分開配置，弩是漢軍在吳楚戰場上最有壓迫感的遠射兵器，張弩壓陣、箭矢齊發，射距遠勝吳楚的步卒。吳楚的兵是江淮、荊楚的鄉土步卒，慣用短刺的戈、矛，人數多而甲少，另有舟師與水軍，沿泗水、淮水、沂水運糧。吳王劉濞的軍中還有銳士與扮作商旅的斥候，騎兵是吳楚聯軍的長處，多來自楚地與淮南的鄉里。漢軍的攻城與野戰工具則極簡：築壁、挖塹、插旗、備車，用車騎步卒的混合大隊作戰，把騎兵放在兩翼，把步卒放在正面。物資方面，關中與河內的粟麥沿驛道與河運往泗水下游，前線的糧食從河南、山東兩面湧來——這正是竇嬰一支偏師能掐住吳楚咽喉的原因。卡面那柄亞述長矛在此役不參戰，它留下的是同一課題：刺擊兵器的柄長與刃形，向來由城牆攻防與密集隊形決定。
kitsEn: The weapons actually carried in this war stand nine and a half centuries away from the Assyrian spear on the card. The Assyrian spear is a short-hafted, long-bladed weapon whose iron point was socketed onto a wooden shaft; it was that form which held the walls of Mesopotamia and that broke through them, and the length of the haft and the shape of the blade were settled by the density of the formation. By 154 BC the line of descent had already forked. The Han foot soldiers carried the ji, a polearm a little over a zhang long that could thrust, hook and also be dropped to strike down, matched with large shields and lamellar armour, so that at close quarters the principle was to out-range the enemy. Shooters were listed separately, bows and crossbows were kept apart, and the crossbow was the most oppressive missile weapon on the Wu-Chu field, its crews cocking and loosing in ranks, and it out-ranged the rebel foot. The troops of Wu and Chu were local levies of the Yangzi and the Jing-Chu lands, accustomed to the short-thrusting ge and mao, numerous but lightly armoured; they also had boat squads and a river fleet that moved grain along the Si, the Huai and the Yi. The army of Liu Pi had hardened assault men and scouts disguised as merchants, and its strength lay in cavalry drawn from the villages of Chu and the lands south of the Huai. The Han field works were of the plainest kind: walls, ditches, flags and wagons, and the mixed column of horse, chariot and foot fought with the horse on the wings and the foot in front. As for supply, millet and wheat from Guanzhong and Henei travelled to the lower Si on the post roads and by river, and food reached the front from two directions, Henan and Shandong; that is exactly why a single detached column under Dou Ying could pinch the rebels' lifeline. The Assyrian spear on the card did not fight in this war. What it records is the same lesson the weapon itself teaches: the length of the haft and the shape of the blade have always been settled by siegework and by the density of the formation.
tactics: 叛軍的打法是典型的聯軍進攻：吳、楚兩國兵多，取正面強攻，分兵趨向梁國睢陽，試圖在漢軍集結之前先拔掉屏障；趙、齊兩國在北方與山東策應，齊國那幾位王又各自打算藉亂擴張封地。吳楚聯軍的優勢在初期的銳氣與對地形的熟悉，劣勢在各自為戰：劉濞與劉戊互相推讓王位，本身就說明聯軍沒有明確的指揮中心。漢軍這邊，周亞夫自有一套次序。他不接吳楚的第一波攻勢，而引兵東北走昌邑，深壁而守，用壘壁把敵人拖在城外；竇嬰的騎兵屯於淮泗之間，斷的是吳楚與其後方之間的粟米通道。吳楚軍遠離根據地作戰，糧道一斷，士卒飢餓，軍心先崩；等聯軍退卻，亞夫才出精兵追擊，在其退路上追而擊之，潰兵為之盡。齊國內部的兵變則完全是另一種樣子：齊王劉將閾與二弟互相攻伐，兵鋒向內，等於自己拆毀了北方的一翼。整場戰役的關鍵，正是「不急於決戰」四個字：漢軍用時間與糧道換掉了吳楚的銳氣，最後以追擊收穫全勝。
tacticsEn: The rebels fought as a coalition army attacks. Wu and Chu, with the mass of men, took the offensive in the front and split their forces towards the principality of Liang at Shihyang, hoping to pull down the screen before the Han troops could assemble; Zhao and Qi supported them from the north and from Shandong, while the Qi kings each meant to enlarge their own territories in the confusion. The Wu-Chu coalition had the advantage of early momentum and of knowing the ground, and the disadvantage of fighting each for himself: the mutual courtesy over the kingship between Liu Pi and Liu Wu shows at once that there was no single command centre. The Han side under Zhou Yafu had its own order of things. He did not accept the first blow of the Wu-Chu army; he marched northeast to Changyi, shut himself in his works and let the enemy exhaust itself in front of the wall, while Dou Ying's horse sat between the Huai and the Si and cut the grain road that ran from the rear of the rebel lines. The Wu-Chu army fought far from its base, and once the supply line was cut the soldiers went hungry and the morale of the ranks broke first; only as the coalition withdrew did Yafu send his picked troops after it, catching and breaking it on the line of retreat, and the fleeing were swept away. What happened inside Qi was the opposite kind of fighting: the Prince of Qi and his two brothers turned their weapons on one another, so that the northern wing destroyed itself. The whole campaign turned on four words: no haste for a decision. The Han army traded time and supply for the momentum of Wu and Chu, and collected the victory in the pursuit.
data: 可考的數字多來自《史記·吳王濞列傳》與《漢書·景帝紀》，多是約數而非實錄。時間上，叛軍在景帝三年正月起兵，戰事同年三月即告收束，前後約三個月；下詔討伐、亞夫出兵的往返與糧草徵發，全都壓在這三個月裡。兵眾方面，《史記》記吳王與諸國之兵眾二十餘萬，這是史家筆下的概數，能集中於前線者顯然少於此；漢軍方面，亞夫將三十六將軍往擊吳楚，竇嬰為大將軍，兩部合計的編制遠小於叛軍，卻握有主動權。城池上，前後有三處要地決定戰局：吳國的會稽郡在起兵前已被削去，叛軍在泗水下游無處可退；梁國睢陽被圍而不下，消耗了吳楚的時間與糧食；昌邑的壘壁則是亞夫手上唯一的一處據點。除人數之外還有一組對照：齊王系的三兄弟自相攻殺而死，吳王首級由東越送來，楚王自縊，七國之王的下場都比不上漢廷的從容，說明聯軍的組織裂痕比兵力差距更要命。武器面上，漢軍是長戟、大盾、弓弩的組合，吳楚是短刺戈矛加舟師的組合，兩套體系的射程與防護不在同一量級。
dataEn: The usable figures come mostly from the Shiji chapter on the Prince of Wu and from the Hanshu chronicle of Emperor Jing, and most of them are approximations rather than counts. In time, the rebels rose in the first month of the third year of Jing and the fighting was over in the third month of the same year, roughly three months in all; the issuing of the order of suppression, the marching of Yafu and the levying of grain and transport all had to fit inside those three months. On numbers of men, the Shiji records the troops of the Prince of Wu and of the other states as 'more than two hundred thousand'; that is a general figure of the time and far more than could be massed in the line, while the Han force — Yafu with thirty-six generals, Dou Ying as General-in-Chief — was much smaller in establishment and held the initiative. Three places decided the campaign. The commandery of Kuaiji had been taken from Wu before the rising, so the rebels had nowhere to fall back to in the lower Si; Shihyang in Liang was besieged and not taken, and the siege consumed the time and the grain of the Wu-Chu army; the works at Changyi were the single fixed point Yafu held. Beyond the head counts there is one telling comparison: three of the kings of the Qi house killed one another, the head of the Prince of Wu came back from Dongyue, and the Prince of Chu hanged himself; not one of the kings of the seven finished better than the court that fought them, which shows that the cracks in the coalition mattered more than the gap in numbers. On weapons, the Han army was a combination of long ji, large shields, bows and crossbows, while Wu and Chu fought with short-thrusting ge and mao and their river fleet; the reach and the protection of the two systems were not of the same order.
cause: 起兵的根由是郡國並行制本身的矛盾。西漢立國時，同姓諸侯王分封到膏腴之地，吳、楚兩國尤其廣大：吳王劉濞的封地與楚王劉戊的封地跨江淮、連荊楚，人眾物產都不亞於中央直轄的郡縣。王國有封土、有賦稅、有自己的官吏，王子並不常入朝；吳王甚至以家中故老自居，長時間不朝。削藩就是要把王國的部分支郡改由中央直接管轄，斷王國的財源與兵源。前154年之前，晁錯已為御史大夫行丞相事，議削諸王：先從楚王劉戊的東海郡下手，再及吳王，理由都擺在明處——吳王已老，其子劉駒年幼，吳國無可用之兵，削之不足懼。景帝二年，削吳王會稽郡的詔令下達，吳王以「賊臣」相號而反，這是導火索。其後晁錯仍主張削到底，理由是王國一日不削，漢廷一日不安。就在同一個朝廷裡，還有另一股力量在為吳國說話：竇氏一族在朝中勢力龐大，梁王劉武既是景帝的同母弟，又與吳王劉濞同出高祖一支，血緣上與吳王最為接近，景帝一時猶豫，議者以為七國既以「誅晁錯、清君側」為辭，殺掉晁錯便可息兵。景帝採納了這個辦法，晁錯被腰斬於市，七國的兵卻沒有停。反叛由此成為七國共同的最後一搏：保住封地不必再靠朝廷恩寵，只要聯軍打倒中央的執政者，王國的存廢就還有自己說的餘地。
causeEn: The root of the rising lay in the contradiction at the heart of the system of commanderies and kingdoms. When the Han was founded, princes of the same clan were enfeoffed in the richest lands, and the states of Wu and Chu above all were vast: the fief of Liu Pi stretched across the Yangzi and the Huai, the fief of Liu Wu across Jing and Chu, with populations and produce in no way inferior to the commanderies administered directly by the centre. A kingdom had its own territory, its own taxes and its own officials, and its princes did not habitually appear at court; the Prince of Wu even put forward the old men of his own household as his justification for seldom paying court. Reducing the fiefs meant taking certain outlying commanderies of the kingdoms back under direct central administration, cutting off their revenue and their source of soldiers. Before 154 BC Chao Cuo had already become Imperial Secretary and was exercising the chancellor's office, and the reduction went ahead: first the eastern commandery of the Prince of Chu, Liu Wu, then the Wu, with the reasoning set openly — the Prince of Wu was old, his son Liu Ju was a child, the state of Wu had no soldiers worth naming, so taking it was no cause for fear. In the second year of Jing the edict stripping the Prince of Wu of the commandery of Kuaiji went out, and the prince called the minister a thief and rebelled; that was the fuse. Chao Cuo still pressed for going further, on the ground that so long as the kingdoms were not reduced the Han court would never be secure. At the same time another interest spoke for Wu inside the court: the Dou clan held great influence at court, and the Prince of Liang, Liu Wu, was both the half-brother of Jing and of the same founding line as Liu Pi, bound to him by blood, so Jing hesitated for a time, and the argument was heard that since the seven states had raised the cry of 'punish Chao Cuo and clear the side of the ruler', killing Chao Cuo would end the war. Jing took that course and Chao Cuo was cut in two at the eastern market, but the armies of the seven did not stop. The rebellion thus became the last common act of the seven: if the coalition could strike down the ministers of state, the continued existence of the kingdoms need no longer depend on the favour of the court.
impact: 平亂之後，漢廷的權威再沒有被諸侯王挑戰過，但王國問題並未因此消失，只是換了一種方式繼續。景帝在吳、楚兩國覆亡之後，態度由寬轉硬：築城、削地、收編支郡的做法一路推到底，連同樣出自同姓的梁國也在中元五年（前150年）被罷去，改作竇氏的食邑，劉武其後抑鬱而終。武帝時的主父偃更把這條路推到終點：元封二年（前115年）的推恩令准許王國把封地分給諸子，於是王國越分越小、越分越碎，父死子繼的說法再也不能保住大國；其後又有元鼎年間以酎金不納為由削爵奪邑的動作，王國終於從帶甲之國變成中央口中的郡。制度之外，事件的教訓也留在政治記憶裡：自秦末到漢初，郡國並行帶來了兩個月的兵禍與大批人力的徵發，於是以後每一次削藩的議論，都要先算一算諸侯的兵力。史家評價七國之亂，大致有兩種：一是把它看作中央集權的關鍵，認為平亂之後削藩不可再緩；二是指出漢廷藉口誅晁錯而用兵，手段並不光彩，對吳、楚兩國的殘酷，超出了鎮壓叛軍的必要。這種兩面性的評價，使它同時成為政治課本與道德教訓的素材。
impactEn: After the revolt was put down, the authority of the Han court was never again challenged by a prince, but the problem of the kingdoms did not vanish; it simply continued in a different form. Once the states of Wu and Chu were crushed, the attitude of Jing hardened from indulgence to firmness: the taking of cities, the reduction of land and the annexation of outlying commanderies was carried through to the end, and even Liang, a state of the same clan, was abolished in the fifth year of Zhongyuan (150 BC) and turned into a grant of food and revenue to the Dou clan, Liu Wu dying before long. Under Emperor Wu the line was taken to its end by the clerk Zhu Yin: the decree of Tui-en in the second year of Yuanfeng (115 BC) allowed a king to divide his fiefs among his sons, so that the kingdoms became smaller and more fragmented with every generation and the claim of inheritance to the eldest could no longer preserve a great state; the forfeiture of titles for failure to offer the gilt gold in the Yuan-ding years, and the annexations that followed, turned the kingdom at last from a state that bore arms into a commandery in the mouth of the centre. Outside the institutions, the lesson stayed in political memory: from the end of Qin to the early Han the coexistence of commanderies and kingdoms had brought two months of war and the levy of a great many men, so that every later debate on reducing a fief had to begin by counting the strength of the princes. Historians judge the Revolt of the Seven States in two ways: as the turning point of central power, holding that once the revolt was over the reduction of the fiefs could no longer be delayed; and as a warning that the court went to war on the pretext of executing Chao Cuo, by means that were not clean, and that the destruction of Wu and Chu went beyond what suppressing a rebellion required. That double reading keeps the event in use both as a lesson in politics and as a case in moral history.
result: 結果是七國全敗，漢廷完勝。吳王劉濞為東越所殺，首級送漢；楚王劉戊自縊而死；齊王劉將閾與二弟膠西王劉、菑川王劉賢同死於彼此攻伐；趙王劉建、濟南王劉辟光相繼被擒或被殺，七國之王無一善終。吳國的宗廟隨劉濞之死而中斷，吳地大部改由郡縣直轄；楚、齊、趙、濟南的封土也陸續被削，漢朝第一次用一次大規模戰役證明諸侯可以舉兵，但諸侯不能取勝。戰役的過程留下兩個可用的樣本：一是周亞夫的戰略，不爭一時的銳氣，據壘以老敵、斷其糧道、待其自退再追擊；二是袁盎的失斷，他以為七國只為誅晁錯，殺掉晁錯便可息兵，七國的兵卻越打越多，直到亞夫掐斷糧道才真正崩潰。晁錯已經腰斬於市，不能復生，景帝為此付出了一次兵禍的代價。從時間上看，這場戰爭只有三個月，卻把西漢此後百年的權力格局定了下來：中央不必再對王國讓步，王國的削弱也從此不再靠一紙詔書，而是靠一場一場可以重複的削奪。
resultEn: The outcome was a complete defeat for the seven and a complete victory for the court. The Prince of Wu, Liu Pi, was killed by the men of Dongyue and his head was sent to Han; the Prince of Chu, Liu Wu, hanged himself; the Prince of Qi, Liu Jianglü, and his two brothers, the kings of Jiaoxi and Zichuan, died in the fighting they turned on one another; Liu Jian of Zhao and Liu Biguang of Jinan were taken or killed in turn; not one of the seven kings escaped. The temple of Wu was broken up with the death of Liu Pi and the greater part of the Wu lands passed under direct commandery administration; the fiefs of Chu, Qi, Zhao and Jinan were likewise reduced in turn, and the Han for the first time proved by one large war that the princes might raise armies but could not win. The campaign left two usable models. The first is Yafu's method: not to contest the enemy's initial momentum, to hold behind works and wear them down, to cut their supply, and to strike in the pursuit once they turned. The second is Yuan Ang's misjudgement: he believed the seven had risen only to have Chao Cuo killed, so that the killing would end the war, and instead their armies grew until Yafu pinched the supply line and the coalition broke for good. Chao Cuo had already been cut in two in the eastern market and could not be restored; the emperor had paid for that misjudgement with a war. In scale the whole rising lasted about three months, and it settled the balance of power for the following century of the Western Han: the centre no longer had to give way to the kingdoms, and from that point the reduction of the kingdoms was no longer something carried by a single edict but by a series of takings that could be repeated.
